# Deployment

Operational notes for running this site outside a local checkout. `npm run
build` produces what is served and `npm run start` serves it; everything below
is what a real deployment target adds around that pair.

## Environments

| Environment | Trigger                     | Notes                            |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Production  | Push to `main`              | Serves the default locale first. |
| Preview     | Pull request opened/updated | One preview per pull request.    |

## Locale fallback

A reader's accepted locales come from their browser's `Accept-Language`
header. `shared/resolve-translation.ts` is what turns that preference list
into the translation a post detail page renders — see its own documentation
for the exact resolution order. Deployment does not change that order; it only
changes which posts and translations the deployed build carries.

## Rolling back

Redeploy the previous commit's build. There is no database to migrate back —
the post catalog and everything else the app reads live in the build itself —
so a rollback here is just a redeploy.

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint

  typecheck:
    name: Type check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck

  test:
    name: Unit tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

  e2e:
    name: End-to-end tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: npm run test:e2e

# tsuzuri

A personal blog: a portrait and bio on the home page, and posts underneath.
Each post can carry more than one translation, and a reader is served
whichever translation best matches the locales their browser sends.

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
```

## Commands

| Command                | What it does                                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`           | Serves the site locally with hot reload.                   |
| `npm run build`         | Builds the production bundle.                              |
| `npm run start`         | Serves a build produced by `npm run build`.                |
| `npm run format`        | Rewrites the project in place to its house style.          |
| `npm run format:check`  | Reports formatting drift without rewriting anything.       |
| `npm run lint`          | Lints the whole project; also checks formatting.           |
| `npm run typecheck`     | Type-checks the project. The test runner compiles without checking types, so this is the only thing that does. |
| `npm test`              | Runs the unit test suite.                                  |
| `npm run test:e2e`      | Runs the end-to-end suite. Builds the app and serves it first, so it needs a browser — `npx playwright install chromium` once per machine. |

## Layout

- `app/(site)/` — the reader-facing route group: the home page, the post
  detail page, and the small data module they both read from.
- `shared/` — code shared by more than one part of the app, independent of any
  one route. `shared/resolve-translation.ts` is the locale-fallback logic a
  post detail page calls into; `shared/blog-post-slug.ts` is the slug shape
  every post's `slug` is validated against.
- `shared/*.spec.ts` — unit tests, colocated with the code they cover.
- `e2e/` — end-to-end specs, kept apart from the unit tests above because they
  exercise the whole running app rather than one module in isolation.
- `docs/` — operational notes that do not belong in code comments, such as
  [deployment](docs/deployment.md).
- `.github/workflows/` — the checks that run on every pull request.

## Contributing

Changes go through a pull request rather than landing straight on `main`.
Before writing code, sketch the plan and get it approved — this catches a
misunderstood requirement while it is still cheap to redirect, rather than
after the diff exists. A pull request is reviewed by someone other than the
person who wrote it, and merges only once that review is clean and the checks
above pass.

content.text:
I found the current rollback note at `docs/deployment.md:22-26` — it's exactly as thin as you said: "redeploy the previous commit's build," full stop. I also checked `ci.yml`, `package.json`, and the app itself for what's actually knowable here, and one thing stood out that's worth fixing while I'm at it:

**The current note has a footgun.** There's no deploy job in this repo's CI — `docs/deployment.md` says production deploys on "push to `main`," which means deploys are driven by an external git-integration (not shown in this repo). If someone rolls back by redeploying an old build *without* also reverting `main`, the next ordinary push to `main` — even an unrelated one — redeploys the broken commit again. A rollback note that doesn't say this will bite someone.

I rewrote the section to fix that, plus add verification steps concrete to this app (there's no health-check endpoint or error dashboard defined anywhere in the repo, so I used what the e2e suite already treats as the app's core contract: post list renders, post pages resolve, unknown slugs 404, locale fallback resolves correctly) and a notify step.

input.new_string:
## Rolling back

There is no database to migrate back — the post catalog and everything else
the app reads lives in the build itself — so a rollback never needs a data
step. But it does need two things to happen together, not just one:

1. **Revert on `main`, don't just redeploy an old build.** Production deploys
   on push to `main`, so if you only redeploy a previous build from
   [hosting platform] without also reverting `main`, the next ordinary push —
   even an unrelated one — redeploys the broken commit again. Open a revert PR
   (`git revert <bad-commit>`, through the normal PR path) so `main` and
   production agree.
   - If the revert can't land fast enough, redeploy the previous build
     directly as a stopgap, but open the revert PR immediately after and
     treat the incident as unresolved until it merges — the dashboard
     rollback alone is not the fix.
2. **Confirm the SHA that's live is the one you meant to roll back to.**
   Check it in [hosting platform]'s deployment details against the commit you
   targeted.

### Verify it worked

There's no health-check endpoint in this app yet, so check by hand:

- `/` loads and lists posts, each linking to `/posts/<slug>`.
- Open one of those post links and confirm it renders the post, not a
  not-found page.
- Visit an unknown slug (e.g. `/posts/does-not-exist`) and confirm it 404s
  instead of erroring — a broken build often surfaces here first.
- If the incident touched translations, check a translated post under a
  couple of different `Accept-Language` values and confirm the result matches
  `shared/resolve-translation.ts`'s fallback order (exact locale → language →
  post default → nothing).
- Watch [error tracking / logs] for a few minutes to confirm whatever error
  rate triggered the rollback has actually dropped.

### Say it happened

Post in [on-call/incident channel]: what was rolled back, the SHA now live,
and a link to the revert PR. Update [incident tracker] so the revert PR isn't
the only record this happened.
